genre_gaps.name: traversal playground
genre_gaps.why: a city built to move through with powers and NPCs, with no fighting stated, has no home - Action is the only genre that owns powers and all four of its shapes are CombatZones, so a movement sandbox was forced into a multi-level arena

genre_gaps.name: social deduction round
genre_gaps.why: the defining feature is a hidden identity among the players, which changes the layout - everyone must spawn together, there is no exit, and cover exists to hide from someone you cannot identify. Survival's 1 vs All was the nearest fit and it assumes a known hunter, so two of its preset options had to be flagged as contradicted

genre_gaps.name: territory control war
genre_gaps.why: a class-based two-faction war over ground is not an arena brawl and not a gunfight; Action owns the melee but has no bases and no territory, Shooter owns the bases and the held point but is built around firing corridors, so the build is stitched from two files and neither shape is right

genre_gaps.name: indoor animal sim
genre_gaps.why: an animal-avatar game set entirely inside one building fits nothing well - Animal Sim assumes open wilderness and dens, Simulation assumes an outdoor shared world, and the housing shapes in Roleplay are all towns

genre_gaps.name: migration journey
genre_gaps.why: a one-way long-haul flight from one real country to another, with weather as the only obstacle, is not a race (no competitors, no clock), not an infinite runner (it ends at a named place) and not an exploration map (there is nothing to find on the way); Adventure's guided corridor was the cheapest available force

genre_gaps.name: lobby front end
genre_gaps.why: the request is only the gathering space of a battle royale with no match map at all - Party and Casual owns the lobby as an option but every preset there bundles a round structure the prompt never asked for, and Shooter Battle Royale would build the island instead of the lobby

genre_gaps.name: target scoring game
genre_gaps.why: a fixed-position projectile game aimed at a target - carnival booth, angry-birds shaped - matches no genre in the index. Party and Casual was the least wrong, and its two shapes are lobby-and-stage or continuous social space, neither of which is a firing line pointed at a target

genre_gaps.name: shooting range game
genre_gaps.why: the game is a static target range wrapped in an incremental money loop, but every Shooter shape and option assumes competitive PvP lanes, bases and objectives, so the classification matches the word 'guns' rather than the game

genre_gaps.name: destruction sandbox
genre_gaps.why: blowing up a structure has no genre; Simulation's Physics Sim was the nearest home but it is about contraptions and ragdolls, and nothing in the index describes a build whose only content is a thing to demolish

genre_gaps.name: turn-based tactics
genre_gaps.why: a move-limited tactical puzzle where you route a piece past opposition to reach a target is neither Strategy's tower-defense-or-RTS framing nor Puzzle's gates-and-key-items framing; Board Grid was forced because it was the only grid in the index

genre_gaps.name: collectathon platformer
genre_gaps.why: a hub-and-realms 3D platformer whose levels are open playgrounds full of hidden collectibles is not an obby course and not an adventure world - Obby owns the movement vocabulary but all three of its shapes are linear courses and its route is P6 procedural generation, while Adventure owns the open-world shape and secret alcoves but has no notion of platform spacing. The concept had to be forced into Obby and patched with Adventure options.

genre_gaps.name: physics stacking game
genre_gaps.why: the entire structure is built by players at runtime out of loose props, and no genre expresses 'empty pad plus a supply of physics objects'; Simulation's Physics Sim was the nearest because it owns physics contraptions, but that preset assumes a designer-authored rig in a persistent world, which is the opposite of what this is

genre_gaps.name: team siege
genre_gaps.why: player-versus-player attack and defend over a fortification fits nothing in the index - Strategy base defense assumes NPC waves and Action arenas are shared clash spaces with no wall, town or asymmetric sides, so Base Defense had to be forced

genre_gaps.name: solo practice arena
genre_gaps.why: an aim-training range is a common Roblox format - one player, one bot, no mode and no win condition. Every Shooter shape and preset assumes competing humans, so the training purpose that is the entire brief is carried by nothing in the emitted block

genre_gaps.name: performance venue
genre_gaps.why: a K-pop concert stage with backstage is not a judging runway, but stage-runway was the only shape in the index carrying a stage at all, so the venue was forced into a fashion-show shape

genre_gaps.name: liminal maze horror
genre_gaps.why: the backrooms is defined by an endless maze with dead ends and no exit; Survival's chase architecture mandates zero dead ends and an escape gate, so the shape on offer is close to the opposite of what was asked for

genre_gaps.name: co-op vehicle expedition
genre_gaps.why: a journey where a shared vehicle is the mobile base and the world streams past it fits no genre - Racing wants a lap or finish line, Simulation wants a job loop, and Adventure's guided corridor describes the road but has no concept of the vehicle or the crew aboard it

genre_gaps.name: ambient nature walk
genre_gaps.why: a purely natural space with no objective, no built content and no hero structure fits nothing cleanly - Adventure requires a focal pull, and Entertainment's showcase presets assume a composed hero build and photo vignettes that a quiet forest does not have

genre_gaps.name: idle clicker room
genre_gaps.why: an idle points game that nonetheless specifies an interior; no genre covers a room that exists only to host a non-spatial loop, so it landed in no-genre

genre_gaps.name: clicker with scenery map
genre_gaps.why: the game loop is entirely on-screen tapping and the map is decoration with no function; every genre in the index assumes the layout carries the gameplay, so Simulation was forced and its whole preset had to be rejected in place

genre_gaps.name: rng collector
genre_gaps.why: the core loop is pressing roll for cosmetic rarity, which no genre in the index names; Simulation's Incremental Simulator was the nearest, but its purchase-gated progression is the opposite of this design's timer-and-luck gating

genre_gaps.name: prison roleplay
genre_gaps.why: Roleplay's shapes are settlements or wilderness; a prison is a secured institution with two opposed roles and an escape objective, so the static-settlement shape stood in for something it was not written for

genre_gaps.name: gang turf roleplay
genre_gaps.why: every housing model in Roleplay is individual - static town, claimable house, personal plot. This game is organised around territory owned by player crews at three purchased sizes, and there is no group-ownership or faction-territory structure anywhere in the index

genre_gaps.name: tabletop object puzzle
genre_gaps.why: a fixed-camera physics pile you pick items out of is neither a maze nor an escape room, and Puzzle's shapes all assume a space you walk through; stage B forced it to P5 even though it has a real 3D set

genre_gaps.name: water ride
genre_gaps.why: drifting downstream on a current is a linear ride the player does not power. Obby and Racing own courses the player drives, Infinite Runner owns automatic motion but is endless and about dodging, and Party owns the social space but not the direction. A river float fits none of them

genre_gaps.name: social deduction game
genre_gaps.why: Party & Casual carries rounds, a lobby and a stage but has nothing for the two structures this genre turns on - a hidden role and a discussion-and-vote phase with its own arena - so the voting courtroom, the most distinctive space in the prompt, had to be written as free text

genre_gaps.name: creative tool game
genre_gaps.why: the game is a shared painting tool in a room; no genre in the index covers player creation, Party & Casual routes Coloring & Drawing to P5 even though this one plainly has a space to walk around in, and no-genre could offer nothing beyond the bare box the user already described

genre_gaps.name: performance venue
genre_gaps.why: a studio where you rehearse and a stage where you perform is a performance venue; the index has exactly one stage, the Dress Up judging runway, so the classification was forced onto a fashion-show shape that has no rehearsal space and no performer-audience relationship

genre_gaps.name: performance venue
genre_gaps.why: the prompt is a stage, a performer and an effects rig the player operates - a venue for a show rather than a place to move through. Entertainment's two showcase shapes are both walk-and-look environments, so the stage had to be forced in as a hero focal build and the audience, the rig and the performer all fell out as free text.

genre_gaps.name: performance venue
genre_gaps.why: Entertainment gives a venue to look at, but this is a creation tool - the player assembles a scene from swappable parts, records it, and competes on the recording. No genre has a shape for a set you configure rather than a map you play in

genre_gaps.name: performance venue
genre_gaps.why: a stage where players perform to a crowd is not an environment to be explored or consumed; Entertainment was the closest fit but its shapes are a guided route, a free-roam space and a portal hub, none of which is a stage plus an audience floor

genre_gaps.name: performance venue
genre_gaps.why: Entertainment presets are architecture you walk around and look at; a festival is a venue with a stage, a performer, and a crowd facing it, and the genre has no stage, audience, or backstage vocabulary - the stage had to be forced into the generic hero-landmark option

genre_gaps.name: music hangout venue
genre_gaps.why: Entertainment's shapes assume a visitor moving through a composed build; a boombox club is a party venue where the players are the content, and no preset offers dance floor plus stage plus lounge

genre_gaps.name: open-world crime city
genre_gaps.why: a drivable, populated city where the player takes on missions and commits crimes matches no genre in the index - Adventure carries the exploration and quest structure but nothing carries vehicles, wanted-level pursuit, or open-ended criminal activity, and Simulation's vehicle options sit under a genre this prompt is not

genre_gaps.name: aerial collection arcade
genre_gaps.why: fly over terrain, grab things, dodge moving hazards — an arcade loop with no tycoon economy, no lap and no combat. Simulation's Vehicle Sim was the least wrong of fifteen, and it brought roads to a game with no roads

genre_gaps.name: vehicle combat
genre_gaps.why: the player is a ship, not an avatar: the map has to be scaled to capital-ship turning and gunnery range rather than a 16 studs-per-second walker, and no genre in the index has vehicles as the combatant

genre_gaps.name: open-world crime city
genre_gaps.why: a GTA-style city sandbox with driving, pedestrians and missions matches no genre in the index; it was forced into Roleplay & Avatar Sim because that is the only genre that owns a prebuilt town

genre_gaps.name: asymmetric pursuit game
genre_gaps.why: two teams sharing one persistent city with opposite win conditions - evade versus capture - fits nothing in the index; Role Sim gave the city and the task stations but says nothing about pursuit, and every Shooter shape assumes a match arena rather than a living world

genre_gaps.name: procedural space sim
genre_gaps.why: the thing to be built is a galaxy — planets, void, space flight, atmospheric entry — and no genre in the index has a shape for any of that. Action was the closest fit because the combat detail is heavy, but its shapes are all bounded clash spaces, so the classification captures the fighting and drops the universe the fighting happens in

genre_gaps.name: open-world crime chase
genre_gaps.why: a persistent city where two factions pursue each other is neither social life-simulation nor a firing-corridor shooter; Roleplay was forced because it is the only genre that owns a town, and the pursuit-and-escape loop the game is actually about has no representation anywhere in the index

genre_gaps.name: movement ability sandbox
genre_gaps.why: an ability-driven free-roam traversal city is not an obstacle course; Obby was the only genre with rooftops and jumps, but every one of its presets assumes an authored linear course with a start and an end

genre_gaps.name: traversal playground
genre_gaps.why: the game is a city built to move through with superpowers, and every Action shape is a bounded collision-clean clash space; there is no genre for an open environment whose content is the movement itself, so a metropolis had to be filed as a multi-level arena

genre_gaps.name: destruction sandbox
genre_gaps.why: no genre in the index has knocking the map down as its point; Simulation Physics Sim was the nearest and it describes ragdoll contraptions and cart rides, so the classification was forced

genre_gaps.name: traversal sandbox
genre_gaps.why: the game is a movement ability in an open city with no objective, score, or opponent - no genre in the index describes free traversal as the point, so it forced to no-genre and the city became free text

genre_gaps.name: animal survival sim
genre_gaps.why: Survival is written around a threat the player evades; here the player is the predator and there is no threat at all, so the whole genre framing had to be inverted to fit a needs-meter wilderness sim

genre_gaps.name: creature taming sim
genre_gaps.why: the prompt is entirely about a roster of creatures you collect, tame or ride, and no genre in the index owns that - Roleplay's Animal Sim is the nearest and it assumes the player IS the animal, so Adventure was taken for the islands and the dragons fell out of the layout completely

genre_gaps.name: creature collection
genre_gaps.why: catching wild creatures across biomes to keep as pets is neither Pet Care (an adoption town), nor Animal Sim (the player is the animal), nor a Simulation production loop; the wilderness shape had to be borrowed and the creatures written as free text

genre_gaps.name: creature collection zoo
genre_gaps.why: buying and displaying collectible animals in your own enclosure is not a tycoon, a sandbox or a pet-care roleplay; Simulation was forced because it owns the shop-and-plot loop, but nothing in the index describes a game whose whole content is exhibits you acquire and look at

genre_gaps.name: developer test scaffold
genre_gaps.why: this is an incremental engineering step, not a game or even a place; stage A had to land on None, and the no-genre options are all about orientation, circulation and social space, none of which applies to an empty baseplate with one spawn part

genre_gaps.name: skate trick sandbox
genre_gaps.why: a skateboarding trick game is a real, common concept but no genre fits: Sports is a scored field with teams, Racing needs laps or a finish line, and Obby is jumping puzzles, so it was forced to no-genre

genre_gaps.name: aerial descent sport
genre_gaps.why: nothing in the index covers a loop whose whole content is falling or gliding downward under control; Obby was forced because it owns towers and skill-based movement, but its three shapes are all ascents or ground courses and its P6 route validates walking jump spacing that this game never uses

genre_gaps.name: tabletop physics game
genre_gaps.why: a block-pulling tower game is a real, popular game concept that no genre in the index covers - the nearest line is Strategy board games, and the space test then refuses it outright even though the scene is plainly buildable

genre_gaps.name: destruction sandbox
genre_gaps.why: the game is wrecking a city for its own sake; Simulation was forced because Physics Sim is the only place breakable assemblies live, but the genre is built around plots, production loops and upgrade hubs and none of those exist here, while Survival owns disasters but assumes you are fleeing them

genre_gaps.name: quiet activity sim
genre_gaps.why: a solitary physics-driven pastime in a natural setting - fishing, hiking, sailing - has no economy, no plot, no round and no opponent, so nothing in the index fits; Simulation was forced and its role-sim task loop is the only piece that attached, dragging hauling roads in with it

genre_gaps.name: shooting gallery
genre_gaps.why: a stationary target-shooting range is neither a PvP shooter map nor a PvE hold-out; shooter.md names gallery shooters as still uncovered and steers them to P5, but there is a real placement job here in where the launchers sit

genre_gaps.name: weapon test range
genre_gaps.why: this is a testbed - one trench, one rifle, one dummy - rather than a game. Every Shooter preset assumes a match with sides or waves, so the nearest fit imports a multiplayer map form the prompt never asked for, and taking no preset leaves the genre contributing almost nothing

genre_gaps.name: training range
genre_gaps.why: a practice facility is recognisably a shooter space but none of the three Shooter shapes fit - there are no lanes between two teams, no breach sequence and no battlefield, just ranges hung off a lobby, and no preset survives contact with a single-player mode with no opponent

genre_gaps.name: lane shooter
genre_gaps.why: a stationary player shooting down auto-advancing lanes fits nothing cleanly - Infinite Runner supplies the scrolling lane geometry but assumes the player dodges, and Shooter assumes a player who walks a map, so the fixed firing position had to be forced into a runner

genre_gaps.name: drift playground
genre_gaps.why: a drifting map is a track built for sustained sliding and scored on style, with no lap requirement and no finish. Racing assumes a finish condition and Simulation assumes a job loop in a persistent world, so neither fits and the shape had to be forced into a lap circuit

genre_gaps.name: finite runner course
genre_gaps.why: forward motion is automatic and lane-based, which is Infinite Runner, but the course has a fixed length and a destination character at the end; the genre is defined as endless and Racing assumes the player controls their own speed, so neither expresses a 30-second runner with an ending

genre_gaps.name: collect and flee sim
genre_gaps.why: the steal-a-brainrot format - grab a creature, outrun a bigger one to safety, plant it on your plot to earn - is one of the largest formats on Roblox right now and it splits cleanly down the middle between Simulation and Survival with neither owning it, so the classification had to pick a half and lose the other

genre_gaps.name: speed progression runner
genre_gaps.why: a stage-based course whose real game is a speed and rebirth economy: Obby holds the geometry but none of its presets, and Simulation owns the incremental loop but has no course shape. The hybrid is a large Roblox category with no home in the index

genre_gaps.name: player-built gauntlet
genre_gaps.why: the tower-defense track happens to give the right spatial furniture, but the roles are reversed - the player authors the hazards and spectates, there is no core to defend and no wave to survive, so the closest genre describes the geometry correctly and the game not at all

genre_gaps.name: interior decorating
genre_gaps.why: a game whose whole play space is one furnished room has no home in the index - Roleplay and Avatar Sim covers houses but all five of its shapes are settlements or a runway, and Simulation sandbox plots are outdoor build lots, so the prompt was routed to no-genre and the room expressed as an enclosure axis

genre_gaps.name: interior decorating game
genre_gaps.why: placing catalog furniture into slots in one room is a real and common game type that matches no genre in the index - it is not a tycoon, not a build sandbox with resources, and not roleplay - so Simulation was forced and its preset had to be part-rejected

genre_gaps.name: creative expression sandbox
genre_gaps.why: the loop is decorating the world itself rather than extracting, building, or running a job; no genre shape or option expresses player-authored surface decoration, so Simulation's shared world was the least-bad fit

genre_gaps.name: trick sports park
genre_gaps.why: extreme-sports trick games - motocross freestyle, skating, BMX - fit nowhere: Racing rules itself out because there is no lap or finish, Sports wants a scored field, and Simulation's Physics Sim is a fallback that describes ragdoll cart rides rather than a park whose ramps are tuned for landable lines

genre_gaps.name: gacha collector game
genre_gaps.why: the game as described is mostly rolling for a collection, which matches no genre in the index and on its own would route P5 for having no space; only the tournament payoff has a court, so Sports ends up owning a prompt it represents about a fifth of

genre_gaps.name: anomaly observation
genre_gaps.why: the game the user is describing is watching a space through cameras and judging what is wrong with it, which no genre in the index covers - Simulation's Role Sim was used because a hospital has a repeatable job loop, and it captures the doctoring while missing the observation the game is actually about

genre_gaps.name: destruction sandbox
genre_gaps.why: the game is destroying objects for tactile feedback and coins - no genre in the index covers object destruction as the loop, so it fell to no-genre and the objects themselves became free text

genre_gaps.name: vehicle as the play space
genre_gaps.why: the only walkable surface in the game is a boat deck floating on empty water; every Simulation shape is a plot or a world laid on ground, and none describes a mobile platform that is itself the map

genre_gaps.name: fishing game
genre_gaps.why: fishing is a large Roblox category and no genre in the index covers it; Adventure's Scavenger Hunt was the closest fit but it treats the catch as a static pickup on land

genre_gaps.name: arcade cabinet venue
genre_gaps.why: the game is played inside a prop, not in the map - no genre in the index covers a venue whose playable content is a machine model; Party & Casual would build minigame arenas the prompt explicitly does not want, and Entertainment's showcase assumes a route through compositions rather than a single object you stand at

genre_gaps.name: creative tool game
genre_gaps.why: the loop is make-art-then-display-it; no genre in the index covers player creation, and Party & Casual explicitly routes Coloring & Drawing to P5, so Entertainment/Showcase was forced onto the gallery half and the painting half produced no layout at all

genre_gaps.name: performance venue
genre_gaps.why: a stage with a crowd in front of it is a real and common build, and no genre owns it - Entertainment's three shapes are a walking route, a free-roam space and a portal hub, none of which encode a stage facing an audience, so the venue had to be forced into a free-roam showcase with the stage demoted to a landmark

genre_gaps.name: performance venue
genre_gaps.why: a concert is a show watched by a crowd, and no genre covers performer-plus-audience; Entertainment was the nearest fit but its presets treat the environment itself as the attraction, so the stage became a focal landmark and the performance dropped out of the handoff entirely

genre_gaps.name: performance venue
genre_gaps.why: A live music festival is a functioning venue - stage, crowd, backstage, vendor rows, restricted areas - not an environment built to be looked at. Entertainment was the nearest genre but its own notes say the landmark there IS the content, which is exactly wrong here: the stage is infrastructure for an event. Sports' stadium shape is closer in form but has a scoring field. It was forced into Free-Roam Showcase.

genre_gaps.name: performance venue
genre_gaps.why: a concert with a stage, a performer, and a seated audience watching a show has no genre. Entertainment was the only place it could land, but Entertainment is about composing an environment for a wandering visitor - it has no stage, no seating, no back-of-house, and its whole premise (free movement toward composed views) is the opposite of an audience facing one direction

genre_gaps.name: rng roller lobby
genre_gaps.why: an RNG or gacha roller is a large and very common Roblox category whose entire loop is a UI button and a rarity table; no genre in the index covers it, so a prompt that specified a full 3D island map had to be forced through no-genre as an undifferentiated social space

genre_gaps.name: video feed hangout
genre_gaps.why: the game is a scrollable user-video feed, which the Entertainment file explicitly routes to P5 as a consumption surface, yet the prompt specifies a full grass map with a fountain, ring path and enterable buildings; the concept had to be forced onto a free-roam showcase to build anything at all

genre_gaps.name: video creation studio

skill_gaps.name: no biome subdivision
skill_gaps.why: the Open World shape is one undifferentiated surface, so three named biomes could only be written as free-text image entries with nothing marking where one ends and the next begins

skill_gaps.name: axes unavailable inside a genre
skill_gaps.why: no-genre can say the play space is volumetric or that water is swimmable; once a genre is chosen there is no equivalent, so 'is the water playable' cannot be expressed

skill_gaps.name: no home for exact counts
skill_gaps.why: 'find 5 coconuts' is the entire goal and the number can only ride along inside the collectible option's free text, so nothing downstream is obliged to place five

skill_gaps.name: no collectible count
skill_gaps.why: a find-the game is defined by how many things there are to find, and neither collectible-nodes nor any handoff field can carry a count or a density

skill_gaps.name: no goal condition field
skill_gaps.why: the entire prompt is a completion goal - find every penguin - and there is no handoff field for a win condition, so it survives only as an open question

skill_gaps.name: pipeline cost has no manual route
skill_gaps.why: bridges over gaps make surfaces stack, which is exactly what P2 exists for, but pipeline modifiers can only arrive attached to a picked option - there is no way to declare one from the prompt, so a genuinely overhanging map emits P0

skill_gaps.name: no channel for screen-space requests
skill_gaps.why: the leaderboard is a HUD element; genre-choice emits only image and layout streams, so it could only be written into notes

skill_gaps.name: invisible collectible geometry
skill_gaps.why: collectible-nodes is tagged layout-only in Simulation, so the berry bushes - the only thing the player actually looks at in this game - never reach the image prompt unless they are re-entered as free text

skill_gaps.name: no home for unlockable roster
skill_gaps.why: the things being found are playable characters with differing abilities, and nothing in the handoff expresses a roster or per-character traits - so the entire reason to explore is invisible to the build, and the map reads as a generic pickup hunt

skill_gaps.name: counts do not survive
skill_gaps.why: the prompt names exactly four animals by species, and once they are promoted to the objective-items option neither the count nor the species list has a field of its own - both survive only inside a free-text string

skill_gaps.name: portal route ambiguity
skill_gaps.why: the Entertainment file flags its own P4 tag on portals as unresolved - portals to separate Roblox places would be P0 - so the single most expensive routing decision in this prompt is decided by a rule the skill says it is unsure about

skill_gaps.name: playable object not a space
skill_gaps.why: every shape in the network describes ground the player moves over, so there is no way to say the layout is scenery around a single interactive prop; the pinball machine, which is the actual deliverable, could only be expressed as a landmark

skill_gaps.name: audio-first games with a space
skill_gaps.why: the genre file says Music and Audio route to P5 because they are content-consumption surfaces with no layout job, but an ASMR walk is audio-first and still has a full environment to build - the rule as written points at a refusal, and only the softer 'judge the concept' note rescues it

skill_gaps.name: no home for persistent player content
skill_gaps.why: the walls fill with art the player generates across sessions, so the build must reserve display space for content that does not exist at generation time and no option or field expresses that

skill_gaps.name: no audio concern
skill_gaps.why: the user names background music as one of six things they want and the handoff has no field for sound at all, so it survives only as an unmatched entry

skill_gaps.name: no channel for external reference
skill_gaps.why: the entire specification is 'lay the stage out like this named real tour', and nothing in the handoff can carry a named external reference for a downstream image model to match against

skill_gaps.name: no home for build constraints
skill_gaps.why: The prompt gives three whole-build instructions - use smooth terrain, be photorealistic, group and label everything in the Explorer - and the handoff has no field for any of them. They ended up in notes, where no downstream step reads them as requirements.

skill_gaps.name: no way to express a scripted scene sequence
skill_gaps.why: three quarters of this prompt is a timeline - portal, show, magic trick, crash, screams, cut to funeral. The handoff emits static spaces with no ordering, no trigger points between them, and no way to say that the same arena has a before-crash and after-crash state

skill_gaps.name: no channel for screen-space requests
skill_gaps.why: the feed and its phone-icon toggle are the point of the game and are pure screen-space, so the central mechanic of the prompt lands in unmatched options with no consumer to receive it

skill_gaps.name: no vocabulary for characters
skill_gaps.why: the whole prompt is a person performing, and the option tables only describe geometry and volumes - there is no way to say a specific character stands here doing this, so the subject of the build had to be smuggled in as an untyped free-text image entry

skill_gaps.name: no building interior option
skill_gaps.why: Entertainment carries no interior or multi-floor option, so a three-story house showcase cannot express its own floors, and the P3 and P2 costs that implies never reach the pipeline field

skill_gaps.name: one prompt, several maps
skill_gaps.why: five built-in settings plus player-built maps is at least six builds, and the handoff carries one shape and one image prompt - the multi-zone axis flags the P4 cost but there is still nowhere to say which map this build is

skill_gaps.name: no player count field
skill_gaps.why: 3v3 is the single most load-bearing number in this prompt - it sets the pitch size, the bench size and the crowd scale - and there is nowhere to put it, so the arena gets sized by a scale band guess instead

skill_gaps.name: no home for match format
skill_gaps.why: 3v3 team size, 3-minute rounds and golden-goal overtime are the spine of this design and directly shape the pitch, but the handoff has no field for goal condition or player count, so they could only be written into notes.

skill_gaps.name: no vocabulary for characters
skill_gaps.why: the referee is a named actor with glowing eyes standing at the centre line and the two gorilla teams are the visible content of the pitch, but the option tables only describe geometry and volumes, so every character had to go in as untyped free text

skill_gaps.name: layout is a fraction of the spec
skill_gaps.why: this is a complete game specification of which one paragraph is a stadium; the intake skill has no way to acknowledge, route or hand off the rules, netcode, minigames, cameras, audio and UI that make up the rest, so a faithful record turns almost the entire prompt into unmatched entries with no consumer

skill_gaps.name: no home for camera specification
skill_gaps.why: a third of this prompt is a precise camera spec - height, follow behaviour, what it must never do - and the handoff has no field for it even though it constrains how the court must be framed and how much run-off space is needed

skill_gaps.name: no home for round or tournament structure
skill_gaps.why: a knockout bracket, a tie-breaker mode, and swap-between-matches rules are all match-state concerns, and the handoff has no key for them, so a build that needs staged rounds gets a single undifferentiated pitch

skill_gaps.name: no home for camera framing
skill_gaps.why: the prompt specifies a fixed top-down view, which decides what the image model should draw and how the field must be proportioned, and there is no field for it - it could only be written into notes

skill_gaps.name: no sport spec field
skill_gaps.why: Sports says regulation dimensions are a known parametric template, but the emitted block has no field naming the sport, so the downstream generator cannot select the template the whole genre depends on

skill_gaps.name: no way to take a named existing map as the spec
skill_gaps.why: the whole prompt is a reference to another game's map, and the skill has a Modelled on column carrying exactly that kind of grounding but forbids surfacing or matching against it. There is no path from 'build me X from game Y' to the preset that was in fact modelled on it, so the reference has to be silently reverse-engineered into options and half of what the name conveys is lost

skill_gaps.name: no home for match format
skill_gaps.why: 'vs' is the only gameplay word in the prompt and it is about team format, which has no field anywhere in the handoff, so a versus soccer match and a solo kick-about emit the same block.

skill_gaps.name: no revision of an existing build
skill_gaps.why: the prompt says the court, not a court - it is an edit to something already built, and intake only knows how to start a layout from nothing

skill_gaps.name: no avatar or character channel
skill_gaps.why: team kits, per-player names and numbers, rig type and seven animation sets are most of what the user asked for, and no destination or field anywhere in the network takes character-level content

skill_gaps.name: no option for the play object
skill_gaps.why: Sports can express the field, the walls, the gates and the scoring plane but not the ball, and here the ball is the most specified thing in the prompt - a light disc locked to chest height, which constrains wall height and gate geometry

skill_gaps.name: no field for player count or team size
skill_gaps.why: pitch proportions and the number of restart positions both depend on how many players are on a side, and nothing in genre-choice or layout-intake carries player count, so the field dimension is an unrecorded guess

skill_gaps.name: no field for player count
skill_gaps.why: a rugby pitch for 7 players and one for 15 are different builds, and the prompt states both. Nothing in genre-choice or layout-intake holds a player count, so the number that should drive field size and spawn count can only be repeated in prose

skill_gaps.name: no lobby in sports genre
skill_gaps.why: the prompt names a lobby as plainly as it names the pitch, and Sports has no gathering-space option of any kind; the only way to keep it was to declare Party & Casual a secondary genre for one option, which overstates the mix and makes the genre list read wrong

skill_gaps.name: no field for player count
skill_gaps.why: the pitch has to be sized for a team count that the prompt varies from one to five a side, and nothing in the handoff carries the number - the same wall hit on the six-player maze prompt, from the opposite direction

skill_gaps.name: pipeline cost stranded on free text
skill_gaps.why: the three-floor enterable lighthouse is the most expensive thing in this build - it forces an inside/outside transition and stacked surfaces - but because no loaded option covers it, it lands as an id:null string that carries no pipeline modifier; I had to add P3 and P2 by hand and say so in notes

skill_gaps.name: no channel for scripted scene content
skill_gaps.why: the memory scenes are the entire content of this map - staged, populated and acting - and the option vocabulary offers only landmarks, collectibles and hazards, so every scene had to be emitted as an id-null image entry

skill_gaps.name: no goal condition field
skill_gaps.why: solving a mystery is the win condition and the handoff has nowhere to put a goal, so the thing the game is about survives only as a clue-node placement

skill_gaps.name: no scene sequence field
skill_gaps.why: this is one place in four states across a story - day clearing, storm, night, then a city - and the handoff has a single shape and a single option list with no way to say which parts exist when, so the ordering could only go in notes

skill_gaps.name: named-game reference has no expansion rule
skill_gaps.why: the prompt's whole description of the experience is a cited title, and nothing in genre-choice says whether to expand a named game into the options that game has or to treat only the literal words as chosen - two readings that produce very different builds, and nothing in the record marks which one was used

skill_gaps.name: no player count field
skill_gaps.why: 'people need to solve it together' is the defining requirement of the prompt and there is no field for co-op, player count, or a puzzle that needs more than one player, so it could only be recorded as a note

skill_gaps.name: no temporal map state
skill_gaps.why: the town visibly degrades across chapters - same footprint, floating buildings, distorted geometry - and the handoff has exactly one shape and one option set, so the only way to express a later state of the same map is world-chaptered, which claims they are separate maps and charges P4 for it

skill_gaps.name: no home for cast and dialogue
skill_gaps.why: nine tenths of this prompt is characters, script beats, choices and endings, and the handoff has no key for any of it - the only way to keep it was as free-text layout entries and unmatched options, so a downstream builder receives an empty school with no indication of what happens in it

skill_gaps.name: licensed world has no home
skill_gaps.why: the whole content specification here is an external reference body - 'the world of Harry Potter' - and no field in the handoff carries a reference world, so what the pipeline receives is a generic chaptered journey with a castle in it. Every recognisable location the user is actually asking for would have to be re-derived downstream or invented wrong.

skill_gaps.name: no goal condition field
skill_gaps.why: the entire prompt is a win condition - get the town to craft a key and escape, then rebirth - and there is no field for it, so it survives only as a note beside a collectible with no owner

skill_gaps.name: scale band cannot hold requested extent
skill_gaps.why: the intake skill picks a band and frames one image, but 100+ connected rooms does not fit any band; the skill says to 'offer the decomposed alternative' and there is no field in the handoff to express a decomposed multi-image build, so the note is the only place it can go

skill_gaps.name: no interior-only expression inside a genre
skill_gaps.why: when the whole map is one building, a genre file can only say building-interior, which means enterable from outside and charges P3; the interior-only enclosure axis that says this cleanly and costs nothing exists only in no-genre, and classifying into a genre gives up access to the axes

skill_gaps.name: no channel for time or day progression
skill_gaps.why: the whole structure of this prompt is a five-day cycle where the same space changes between days - nothing in the shape, option, or handoff schema can express a map that has states over time, so day five's mall and day one's mall are the same emitted layout

skill_gaps.name: one shape for two maps
skill_gaps.why: this prompt describes a Party and Casual lobby feeding a separate Adventure school, and each half wants its own shape. The rule that the dominant genre owns the shape forced the lobby to be expressed as loose options under a Chaptered Journey, so the mode-select staging area, which is a third of what the user wrote, has no structural representation at all

skill_gaps.name: no player spawn option
skill_gaps.why: Adventure has no spawn marker in its option table at all, only Survival carries spawn-protected, so the single most explicit spatial fact in the prompt had to be written as an id-null layout entry

skill_gaps.name: no character or npc field
skill_gaps.why: a large share of the prompt is one character and her exact outfit, and there is no option, field or stream for characters anywhere in the network - it had to go into image_prompt as raw free text

skill_gaps.name: no platform convention library
skill_gaps.why: the whole prompt is a shorthand reference to a known Roblox format, and nothing in the skill can record match this convention, so a preset stood in for it and every other field was invented or asked

skill_gaps.name: no scene or act sequence
skill_gaps.why: this is a linear story that visits five distinct spaces in a fixed order, and one of them replaces another mid-game; the handoff has a single shape and a flat option list with no ordering, so the entire structure of what the user described - the sequence itself - has no field to live in

skill_gaps.name: no scene sequencing
skill_gaps.why: the prompt is an ordered script of eleven scenes where order and re-visiting the same room in a changed state are the whole design, and the handoff can only emit an unordered set of places - the sequence survives only as a free-text note

skill_gaps.name: no home for the camera vantage
skill_gaps.why: this prompt spends its first sentence fixing the viewpoint - elevated first-person, not top-down - and the layout pipeline's whole premise is drawing a top-down or isometric image. A stated camera is a hard constraint on how much the terrain may occlude, but there is no field for it and it survives only as free text in notes

skill_gaps.name: no home for camera framing constraint
skill_gaps.why: a fixed top-down view that must make a 3D scene read as 2D dictates elevation, silhouette and map proportions, but layout-intake owns only genre, theme and scale, so the single most binding requirement in this prompt could only be written as a note

skill_gaps.name: scale band loses exact dimensions
skill_gaps.why: the user specified a 120x120 stud arena and a 9-12 stud lane width, and the only field for extent is a four-way band; 'block' covers 100-500 studs, so the numbers that make this arena the arena survive nowhere in the handoff

skill_gaps.name: no goal condition field
skill_gaps.why: survive wave 10 to win and lose at zero base health is the stated core of the game, and nothing in genre-choice or layout-intake holds a win or loss condition, so it could only be dropped into free-text notes

skill_gaps.name: no channel for asset-generation method
skill_gaps.why: the user gave a direct instruction about how every asset must be produced - mesh_generation for enemies, towers, portal, castle - and the handoff has no field for asset provenance, so a pipeline-level directive can only be smuggled through notes and may simply be ignored

skill_gaps.name: no home for a separate lobby map
skill_gaps.why: the prompt spawns you in a building, has you roll and equip units there, then teleports you to the battlefield; the dominant genre owns exactly one shape, so the lobby, the teleport link, and the P4 and P3 cost of a second interior map cannot be expressed and land in notes

skill_gaps.name: no player-alterable path
skill_gaps.why: maze tower defense is a whole subgenre and the only lane shape is defined as unchanging; there is no way to express 'the route is recomputed at runtime' and P6 cannot validate a path that has not been built yet

skill_gaps.name: no per-player plot outside simulation
skill_gaps.why: isolated per-player plots exist only as a Simulation shape, so a Strategy-dominant multiplayer prompt where everyone has their own base cannot express it

skill_gaps.name: no lobby in strategy
skill_gaps.why: Obby and Simulation both carry social-hub, Strategy does not, yet the lobby-plus-elevator hub is standard to every Roblox tower defense game and is most of the buildable geometry here; it had to be written as untyped free text

skill_gaps.name: no multi-map handoff
skill_gaps.why: one lobby plus seven themed match maps are requested; the block holds a single shape, preset and option set, so P4 records that separate frames exist while the seven themes are reduced to one line of free text

skill_gaps.name: no channel for a named reference game
skill_gaps.why: half of this prompt is the name of another game used as the visual spec, and the handoff has no field for it - the internal Modelled on column is the only place references live and it is explicitly not allowed out

skill_gaps.name: no economy or progression field
skill_gaps.why: buying and upgrading units with money is stated three times in a one-sentence prompt and there is nowhere in the handoff for an economy, so the whole request survives only as a note

skill_gaps.name: one shape cannot cover hub plus instanced maps
skill_gaps.why: the prompt describes a lobby and the separate battle maps it teleports into, which are two different layouts with different shapes. genre-choice emits exactly one shape, so the lobby survives as a couple of options bolted onto a battle-map shape, and the part the user said mattered most gets the least of the handoff

skill_gaps.name: no multi-map support
skill_gaps.why: the prompt asks for four distinct themed maps and no genre offers a multi-map shape. Three of the four environments simply vanish from the handoff, and the P4 code exists in the pipeline vocabulary with no option or shape in Strategy that can emit it

skill_gaps.name: no multi-map handoff
skill_gaps.why: one lobby plus seven themed match maps are requested; the block holds a single shape, preset and option set, so P4 records that separate frames exist while the seven themes are reduced to one line of free text

skill_gaps.name: no home for unit and economy design
skill_gaps.why: about eighty per cent of this prompt is soldier stats, damage rates, crate purchases, an inventory and a wave-unlock ladder. None of it has a consumer in the handoff, so it all lands in unmatched_options tagged progression or mechanics, and the parts that do shape the map, such as how many blocks a player can place, cannot influence the layout at all

skill_gaps.name: no trigger volume in strategy
skill_gaps.why: Strategy has BuildZone but no trigger or dwell volume, and this prompt's entire interaction model is standing on a tile for 2 seconds; the build pads could be expressed and the tiles that operate them could not

skill_gaps.name: no lobby in strategy
skill_gaps.why: the prompt opens with a lobby, elevators, match status and map select, and Strategy's option table has no hub, lobby or staging area at all - its shape is the enemy lane and nothing else. Party and Casual has exactly the option needed, but a correct single-genre classification cannot reach it, so the first section of the prompt lands entirely in free text

skill_gaps.name: no channel for screen-space requests
skill_gaps.why: roughly four fifths of this prompt is menus, HUDs and system behaviour; the handoff has one place to put a request and every one of them had to be logged as unmatched rather than routed anywhere

skill_gaps.name: no player count field
skill_gaps.why: the map has to hold several players placing towers without overlap, which is a direct sizing input for the build, and nothing in the handoff can carry it

skill_gaps.name: escalating speed invalidates fixed spacing limits
skill_gaps.why: Obby derives all platform spacing from default WalkSpeed and JumpHeight, so a course whose whole design is the player accelerating cannot be validated by P6; Infinite Runner has elastic speed-derived spacing for exactly this and Obby has no way to borrow it

skill_gaps.name: no field for player count
skill_gaps.why: the prompt is explicitly about doing this with other players and nothing in the handoff records how many people share the space or that it is social rather than solo

skill_gaps.name: no goal condition field
skill_gaps.why: reaching the flag is the win condition and the only option that can carry it is an end reward area, so the handoff records a reward the user never asked for and records the goal nowhere

skill_gaps.name: no home for runtime world states
skill_gaps.why: eight admin-triggered events reshape the space at runtime (lava rising, fog, darkness, low gravity), and the handoff describes one static map with no field for alternate states of it

skill_gaps.name: no home for course length
skill_gaps.why: the most specific thing in the prompt is a number - 300 stages across five worlds - and nothing in the handoff can hold it. Shape says tower, scale says a band in studs, and neither expresses how long the course is, so the count survives only as a note

skill_gaps.name: cannot ask the one clarifying question
skill_gaps.why: stage A lands on Unrecognised, and the only remedy the skill offers is a single question; with no human in the loop the rule falls through to no-genre, so a two-word prompt quietly produces a generic place rather than the tower the user had in mind

skill_gaps.name: scale band is horizontal only
skill_gaps.why: the bands measure ground extent, and a tower's defining dimension is height - 'block' says nothing about whether this is a 200-stud or 2000-stud climb, which is the only number this prompt actually needs

skill_gaps.name: no goal or win condition field
skill_gaps.why: reach the top, kill every boss, then take the key is both the win condition and the ordering rule that shapes the whole tower, and layout-intake names goal as a required spatial field with no current home. It survives only as free text and a note

skill_gaps.name: no multi-map route
skill_gaps.why: genre files have no equivalent of no-genre's multi-zone axis, so several separate selectable maps cannot raise the pipeline to P4 or be represented as more than one map

skill_gaps.name: preset outweighs prompt
skill_gaps.why: a three-word prompt produced four options, all of them the preset's; the brief's own measure of preset padding is maximal here and nothing in the skill flags that the build is now mostly invention

skill_gaps.name: no dynamic re-theming
skill_gaps.why: theme is a single string in the handoff, so a build whose entire hook is transforming from cozy to horror mid-session can only be expressed as one theme with a note

skill_gaps.name: no avatar or morph concern
skill_gaps.why: intake covers genre, theme, and scale, so a request about what the player wears has no field to land in, and the closest option (social-hub) is a shop lobby that only accidentally fits

skill_gaps.name: no channel for audio
skill_gaps.why: music, per-object sound and video playback are most of what this user asked for and the handoff has no audio or media stream, so they can only be logged as gaps

skill_gaps.name: no expression for endless space
skill_gaps.why: every scale band is a bounded extent and the pipeline frames one image, so a course that by definition has no end can only be recorded as a note - nothing in the handoff says generate this forever

skill_gaps.name: stacked floor tower has no shape
skill_gaps.why: a tower of enclosed rooms stacked vertically and gated one at a time is a common Roblox format, and no shape in either loaded genre says it - Action's arena-chain is horizontal, Obby's course-tower is a platform ascent with no rooms, so the defining structure of this prompt survives only as a note

skill_gaps.name: no per-segment decomposition
skill_gaps.why: layout-intake says to offer a decomposed alternative when a tower will not fit one top-down frame, but neither the handoff nor the genre-choice block has a field for 'N stacked segments', so the only correct answer to a 67-floor tower is a note the pipeline cannot act on

skill_gaps.name: no linear zone chain shape
skill_gaps.why: RPG offers one contiguous surface, a hub feeding instanced dungeons, or a distance-scaled open world; a linear pilgrimage of handcrafted zones is none of the three, so the closest shape misdescribes the world as open when the prompt insists it is linear

skill_gaps.name: preset shape versus stated shape
skill_gaps.why: the closest preset by game type carries a shape the prompt overrides — a turn-based creature collector on a single map, against a prompt that names a village, a wilderness and a dungeon. The skill says the preset is a shape plus options and also says never to re-ask what the prompt already answered, and gives no rule for which wins

skill_gaps.name: no goal condition field
skill_gaps.why: the only stated objective is collecting points at events, and there is no field for a goal or scoring condition, so the handoff cannot say what the zoo is for

skill_gaps.name: no production chain option
skill_gaps.why: a tycoon is defined by its droppers, conveyors and income-producing machinery, and Simulation offers only a purchase gate, a shop hub and circulation; the word 'tycoon' therefore produces a plot with a gate and a store and nothing that actually produces anything, which is the one thing the user named

skill_gaps.name: no stat-gated progression
skill_gaps.why: the course difficulty curve is a stat requirement, not a spacing requirement, and nothing in the handoff can say a stage is locked behind a speed value; worse, P6 validates gaps against default WalkSpeed, which this game deliberately breaks

skill_gaps.name: no home for progression and economy
skill_gaps.why: the entire tycoon loop here is a timer paying a currency into eight unlock tiers, and the handoff can only say there are eight slots - the payout, the tier costs and the session lengths all fall out

skill_gaps.name: no channel for animated scenery
skill_gaps.why: the user's one adjective for the map is 'animated', and every option in the network describes static geometry - there is no field anywhere in the handoff that says a piece of the map should move, so the request can only be smuggled into free text an image model may or may not honour

skill_gaps.name: no building in simulation
skill_gaps.why: a tycoon is almost always a building being assembled, and Simulation has plots, gates, paths and hubs but no option that says 'a structure'; the one concrete noun in the prompt had no home

skill_gaps.name: no channel for progression economy
skill_gaps.why: coins, XP, levels, prestige, pets, quests and gamepasses are most of this 900-word prompt and none of it has a home; the handoff hands downstream a map with no indication that the map exists to serve an upgrade ladder, and the ten worlds - the single biggest cost driver here - can only be expressed by inventing a pipeline modifier

skill_gaps.name: no home for ux design constraints
skill_gaps.why: roughly half this prompt is non-negotiable interface ethics - neutral choice presentation, no pre-checked toggles, cost disclosure, no nagging - and the skill network has no concern that carries a constraint over the whole product, so it can only be dropped into free-text notes where no downstream consumer will act on it

skill_gaps.name: no home for exact counts
skill_gaps.why: 'exactly 6 plots' is the single most load-bearing fact in this prompt and the emit block has no field for a count - the shape says isolated per-player plots but not how many, so the number survives only inside free text where a later step may or may not honour it

skill_gaps.name: no economy field
skill_gaps.why: the payoff of the whole loop is that delivered brainrots earn money, and nothing in the handoff can carry an economy - it survives only as a note, so a downstream build has no reason to give the base a payout point at all

skill_gaps.name: no economy or progression channel
skill_gaps.why: rarities, upgrades, prestige, pets and the collection book are the substance of the design and none of them have a home, so a fourteen-entry unmatched list is doing the work the handoff should

skill_gaps.name: dominant shape excludes secondary need
skill_gaps.why: the dominant genre owns the shape, so taking Tycoon's shared plot means the Strategy half of the request loses the open contested terrain it needs; an army you can command has nowhere to march to, and the rule offers no way to keep both without smuggling in a second shape

skill_gaps.name: preset shape is not separable
skill_gaps.why: a preset is a shape plus options and must be taken whole, but the prompt accepted the Tycoon options while contradicting its shape; there is no sanctioned way to keep the preset and swap the housing model, so the shape had to be overridden silently

skill_gaps.name: no home for player count
skill_gaps.why: six bases 'for players to select' is a statement about how many people the map serves, and there is no field for player count - the number only survives as free text, so nothing downstream knows whether to size the map for six or for sixty

skill_gaps.name: no per-zone theme
skill_gaps.why: the map is a set of bases each themed to a different film and theme is one string in the handoff, so the field had to be filled with a compound description no consumer can apply base by base - the same wall the four-biome open world hits

skill_gaps.name: no district zoning
skill_gaps.why: a city prompt is fundamentally about grouping the map into residential and commercial areas, and Simulation's shapes are all plot-or-world scoped with no way to say the map subdivides into themed districts

skill_gaps.name: no player count field
skill_gaps.why: limited people 4 players sizes the whole build - it decides shared plot versus isolated plots and the extent of the street loop - and there is no field for player count, so it survived only as a constraint entry

skill_gaps.name: no channel for screen-space requests
skill_gaps.why: this prompt is a thousand-point specification of which roughly sixty items are GUI frames and three hundred are data records; the handoff can accept none of it, so a lane executing it honestly produces a nearly empty layout and a very long gap list, with no way to tell the user that most of what they wrote was never ours

skill_gaps.name: free text cannot set pipeline
skill_gaps.why: a fifteen-floor stacked base is exactly what P2 exists for, but because no option covers a multi-storey base the request landed as free text and the emitted route says P0

skill_gaps.name: shape and preset coupled
skill_gaps.why: the prompt names an underground garage, and the only shape that expresses a layer beneath the surface belongs to a mining preset; picking the correct shape therefore costs the preset entirely and every option has to be hand-picked

skill_gaps.name: no water play medium
skill_gaps.why: the entire buildable surface is water that is swum through, launched off and grinded along; the option tables treat water only as a hazard, so the one thing the layout has to get right has no representation

skill_gaps.name: no goal condition field
skill_gaps.why: passing the level is defined entirely by where the crate lands, and the handoff has no goal field, so the win condition survives only as a note and an unmatched entry

skill_gaps.name: no goal condition field
skill_gaps.why: reaching the exit is the entire win condition and the handoff has no goal field; with no loaded option for a terminal exit it could only be written as an id-null free-text entry

skill_gaps.name: no build scope field
skill_gaps.why: there is no way to say build only this part of the game, so the preset supplied a full deathmatch map for a prompt that explicitly deferred it - the emitted handoff describes more than the user asked to exist

skill_gaps.name: no scripting deliverable channel
skill_gaps.why: the user's first and most explicit ask is a teleportation script, and intake has no way to record a request whose deliverable is code rather than a map - it is silently dropped and the layout half is answered as though it were the whole question

skill_gaps.name: no way to express access rules
skill_gaps.why: a locked door is neither geometry nor a placed volume; it is a permission on a doorway. It is the single most load-bearing word in this prompt and there is no option, type, or field that carries it, so it survives only as free text

skill_gaps.name: no home for per-player plots in a shared world
skill_gaps.why: the handoff has one map, one shape and one scale band, so a persistent neighbourhood where 20-40 players each own a base and can walk between them has nowhere to be expressed

skill_gaps.name: biome gradient forces separate maps
skill_gaps.why: the only shape that expresses difficulty scaling with distance also declares the regions separate maps and charges P4, so a prompt asking for one seamless world with a difficulty gradient cannot be expressed without either lying about the shape or contradicting the user

skill_gaps.name: no round structure field
skill_gaps.why: a 5-minute round is stated plainly and is load-bearing for how big the arena can be, but there is no field for round length - it survives only as free text in notes

skill_gaps.name: multi-map builds have no home
skill_gaps.why: a lobby plus N randomly chosen maps is one request but the skill emits one shape, one image and one option set; the P4 separate-maps cost sits on a secondary genre shape that the dominant-genre rule forbids taking, so it had to be added to the pipeline by hand

skill_gaps.name: threat type is unasked
skill_gaps.why: survival shape hinges entirely on whether the threat is a region, an actor, or nothing, and the workflow allows only one clarifying question and only for an Unrecognised stage A - a clearly-classified Survival prompt with no stated threat gets no question at all

skill_gaps.name: no player count field
skill_gaps.why: the prompt is almost entirely about choosing between one and five players, and nothing in the handoff records how many players the space is for, even though it drives island size, spawn count and threat scaling

skill_gaps.name: no water surface concept
skill_gaps.why: every shape and option in the loaded file assumes walkable or drivable ground; a prompt whose headline vehicle is a jet ski cannot say that half the map is water, so the option had to be emitted with a null id

skill_gaps.name: no channel for incremental additions
skill_gaps.why: the prompt says 'Add a casino lounge', which extends an existing build, and intake only knows how to classify and generate a whole map from a prompt - there is no field for what it attaches to or where, so the handoff reads as though a casino lounge were the entire game

skill_gaps.name: no vocabulary for interior rooms
skill_gaps.why: the tables can express an enterable building as a whole but have no way to name the rooms or fixtures inside it, so both of the only two things this prompt asked for fall out as free text

skill_gaps.name: no channel for supplied assets
skill_gaps.why: the skill network assumes the map is generated from a description; there is no field anywhere in the handoff for prebuilt asset ids the user wants inserted verbatim, and no way to express that generation should be skipped, so the request survives only as a note and the emitted block describes a build nobody asked for

skill_gaps.name: no channel for exact object spec
skill_gaps.why: The user gave literal coordinates, part sizes, object names, counts and script behaviour. The handoff has no field for any of it - option text is descriptive prose meant for an image model - so a prompt that was fully specified arrives downstream as vague geometry, which is the one outcome this request cannot tolerate.

skill_gaps.name: no vegetation option
skill_gaps.why: neither no-genre nor the loaded tables have any option for natural cover - trees, forest, terrain - so the bulk of what this prompt asks for can only travel as free text

skill_gaps.name: no outcome for an unparseable prompt
skill_gaps.why: stage A offers Genre, Mixed, Unrecognised and None, all of which assume the prompt is understood. This one is barely grammatical and the only honest answer is that we do not know what was asked, which the skill can only express as P5 or None - both of which read as confident determinations

skill_gaps.name: no terrain or biome vocabulary
skill_gaps.why: the entire prompt is a biome — desert — and nothing in genre-choice or layout-intake carries ground type; theme covers mood and materials but not whether the ground is sand, snow or grass, so the only load-bearing word in the prompt had to ride as an id-null free-text entry

skill_gaps.name: no npc character field
skill_gaps.why: the character is the subject of the whole prompt and there is no key for her - she could only be written as a free-text image entry, where a segmenter will treat her as scenery

skill_gaps.name: no audio concern
skill_gaps.why: the only feature the user actually specified is an audio behaviour - a mic that plays your voice back - and intake has no concern, field, or destination for sound at all, so the single distinguishing request in the prompt survives only as an id-null prop

skill_gaps.name: no lighting channel
skill_gaps.why: shadows, glare and light quality are the whole request, and neither the image options nor the layout options can carry lighting or render settings - the handoff has nowhere to put it but a note

skill_gaps.name: no home for exact counts
skill_gaps.why: 75 lifeboats, two funnels and two masts are the entire specification and the handoff carries counts only as prose inside a text string, where nothing downstream can act on them

skill_gaps.name: preset padding on minimal prompts
skill_gaps.why: step 3 says match the closest preset and offer it, but gives no threshold for when none fits; on a prompt asking for a plain place every no-genre preset would have added a landmark, a path and a scenic vantage, so the preset had to be declined on judgement rather than by rule

skill_gaps.name: theme-only prompt produces empty layout
skill_gaps.why: the entire prompt is a theme, and layout-intake declares theme to be set dressing that never changes the route, so everything the user actually said lands in a field marked non-load-bearing while the layout content comes wholly from a default preset; no-genre also has no option for the built fabric itself, only for landmarks, paths and scenic spots

skill_gaps.name: no exterior-only building option
skill_gaps.why: the only structure option in no-genre is building-interior, which means enterable and costs P3, so a village of houses you only see from outside has no id and has to travel as free text

skill_gaps.name: lobby keyword vs no game
skill_gaps.why: the genre index lists lobby as a Party and Casual recogniser, but a bare lobby prompt names no rounds, minigames, or exits to anywhere; stage A had to choose between a genre fired by one keyword and no-genre, and nothing in the rules settles which - the two answers produce different shapes

skill_gaps.name: no per-element colour field
skill_gaps.why: theme is one free-text string for the whole build, so a prompt whose entire content is which colour each part is has nowhere to put it except the option text

skill_gaps.name: no channel for a named reference
skill_gaps.why: eleven words, and the load-bearing one is a title. Everything the user wants about the look lives inside that reference, and the only place it can go is a free-text theme string that no downstream step is obliged to honour

skill_gaps.name: no home for endless extent
skill_gaps.why: the request is that the space never ends; the handoff describes one bounded framed surface and has no field for tiling, repetition, or procedurally continuing geometry

skill_gaps.name: no option for interactive prop
skill_gaps.why: a keycap that reacts to being touched is neither drawable-only geometry nor an invisible volume - it is both at once, and step 5's image-or-layout rule forces it to be written twice with nothing tying the two halves together

skill_gaps.name: no real-world location reference
skill_gaps.why: Delhi is the entire content of the request and there is no field to carry a real-world place, so it survives only as free text in the theme string

skill_gaps.name: no channel for sky and lighting
skill_gaps.why: the starry space skybox is one of five things the user asked for and there is no field in the handoff that owns skybox, weather, or global lighting, so it can only be written into notes

skill_gaps.name: hub ambiguity
skill_gaps.why: Entertainment carries two readings of the word hub at very different pipeline costs - portal hub at P4 and free-roam space at P0 - and the genre file has no rule for choosing between them when the prompt just says hub. Its own notes flag this as an open question and then leave it to the reader

skill_gaps.name: no incremental edit to existing build
skill_gaps.why: the request adds one feature to a scene that already exists and positions it relative to the user's viewpoint; the intake assumes a whole map generated from nothing, so there is no field for what is already there or for where the user is standing

skill_gaps.name: no handling for clone-by-reference
skill_gaps.why: the prompt is entirely a pointer to an external title, and the network has no step that resolves a named game into layout content - the Unrecognised branch only offers to ask a question, which a batch run cannot do and which a user who just said 'the same as X' has already implicitly refused to answer

skill_gaps.name: no sky or lighting field
skill_gaps.why: the pink sunset is half of what the user asked for, and the handoff has no skybox, time-of-day, or lighting key - it could only be smuggled in as an untyped image entry

skill_gaps.name: no channel for screen-space requests
skill_gaps.why: the admin panel is the second of three things the user asked for and is entirely a GUI with permissions attached; it had to be emitted with a null id or dropped, and a downstream reader cannot tell it is not meant to be built as geometry

skill_gaps.name: no field for map footprint
skill_gaps.why: the whole request is the plan shape of the map - round, not square - and neither the no-genre axes nor any option carries footprint, so it survives only as a free-text image entry that the image model may ignore

skill_gaps.name: defining feature carries no option
skill_gaps.why: the one thing the user asked for has no option anywhere, so the handoff is three preset options nobody requested plus a single free-text line doing all the work. The preset-acceptance rule makes the record look fuller than the prompt was

skill_gaps.name: no authored floor plan channel
skill_gaps.why: the user handed over an exact top-down layout and a construction spec, and the handoff has nowhere to put an authored plan - it can only be paraphrased into notes, where the image stage is free to ignore it

skill_gaps.name: no vegetation or terrain option
skill_gaps.why: trees and hills are the entire content of this prompt and neither has an option anywhere in no-genre.md, so the two things the user actually asked for both land as id:null free text

skill_gaps.name: no vegetation option
skill_gaps.why: forest density and flower ground cover are the entire content of this prompt, and no option in any loaded file describes flora, so the thing that defines the map can only ride along as free text

skill_gaps.name: no landform option
skill_gaps.why: every options table places features onto an assumed surface; nothing names the base terrain, so the mountain the user actually asked for has to ride in as free text

skill_gaps.name: no channel for screen-space requests
skill_gaps.why: roughly nine tenths of this prompt is a ScreenGui specification - frames, fonts, buttons, mobile scaling, a reference screenshot - and the handoff has nowhere to carry any of it, so a faithful record of the request survives only as unmatched_options

skill_gaps.name: asset sourcing not expressible
skill_gaps.why: the user's most emphatic instruction, repeated three times, was about how assets must be produced; the handoff has no field for asset-sourcing constraints so it survives only as a note

skill_gaps.name: single object is not a map
skill_gaps.why: the request is one modelled vehicle with a required part hierarchy, not a place; every genre including Entertainment assumes a walkable environment, so the showcase shape and its spawn/vignette options were fitted around an object that may never be entered

skill_gaps.name: no home for goal condition
skill_gaps.why: go through a dark forest is a win condition and nothing else; the handoff has no key for it, so the one thing the user actually specified survives only as a shape choice and an open question

skill_gaps.name: build-tool directive has no home
skill_gaps.why: half this prompt is the user telling us which generation primitives to use; it is a real instruction about how the build happens, but layout-intake has no concern for tooling and it can only be logged as a note

skill_gaps.name: no home for vehicle capacity
skill_gaps.why: 'holds 8 passengers' drives how many rescue points a trip clears and how densely they should be placed, and no field carries it into the build

skill_gaps.name: no vertical play volume
skill_gaps.why: every shape in the genres reached here is a ground surface or a plot; a game played in the air above a set of buildings has no shape that says the play space is the volume rather than the ground

skill_gaps.name: lapless driving is homeless
skill_gaps.why: Racing's boundary rule sends any driving game without a lap or finish to Simulation's Vehicle Sim, which is written around cooperative machinery work and hauling resources; a plain 'drive a nice car on nice roads' prompt lands there and picks up an extraction field it has no use for

skill_gaps.name: no channel for performance budget
skill_gaps.why: 'low graphics so poor devices can play' is a hard constraint on the whole build - poly count, texture size, draw distance - and the handoff has only theme, which describes look rather than cost, so the one requirement the user repeated cannot be passed to the pipeline

skill_gaps.name: no moving hazard
skill_gaps.why: hazard-kill is written as a static damaging region with a shape and a boundary, but a tornado travels the length of the map and the whole layout is built around where it can gain speed

skill_gaps.name: no channel for audio
skill_gaps.why: the CC201 engine sound is one of four things the user named and there is no audio stream anywhere in the handoff, so it survives only as a note

skill_gaps.name: prompt continues an earlier turn
skill_gaps.why: the prompt starts with Of course and reads as a reply inside a conversation the skill cannot see; there is no field anywhere in the handoff to record that the request is a fragment, so the build silently treats a half-sentence as a full spec

skill_gaps.name: playable space is a moving vehicle
skill_gaps.why: the play area is the interior of a bus travelling along a road, so the build is a static road plus a moving room; no shape, option or pipeline code can express a play volume that moves relative to the map, and the seats inside it have no option either

skill_gaps.name: no asset-source constraint field
skill_gaps.why: use models from the Roblox store is a build-wide instruction about how geometry is produced, and the handoff has no place for constraints on the production method

skill_gaps.name: no option for ambient npc population
skill_gaps.why: AI pedestrians and AI traffic are half of what this user asked for, and every spawner option across the loaded genres means hostiles or waves - there is no way to place non-hostile ambient life, so the entire request fell to free text

skill_gaps.name: no progression concern
skill_gaps.why: intake has concerns for genre, theme and scale only. 'You get $10 when you drive' is the entire loop of this game and it lands in gaps with no consumer, while the garage lobby that exists to spend it survives only because a hub option happened to fit

skill_gaps.name: multi-map request has no route
skill_gaps.why: the prompt asks for ten named environments and nothing in the skill decides between one world and ten maps - P4 exists as a pipeline code but only a shape can carry it, and no Simulation shape does, so a request for ten maps can only be honoured by silently reclassifying the game

skill_gaps.name: prompt defined by reference title
skill_gaps.why: the entire request is 'like game X but bigger', and nothing in the skill network resolves a game title into layout content, so the classification rests on one ambiguous word

skill_gaps.name: no guided-track path type
skill_gaps.why: path-road-vehicle is the only circulation option that fits rail, but a road is free-form and track is a fixed guideway with grade and curve-radius limits. Bending the text loses the constraint that actually makes a rail map buildable.

skill_gaps.name: no goal condition field
skill_gaps.why: win is stopping the train before ten minutes, loss is a scripted derailment at a named place on the map; the handoff has no field for either, so the load-bearing part of the design lives only in notes

skill_gaps.name: no real-world location reference
skill_gaps.why: the map is a named real street in a named real city, deliberately distorted, and there is no field carrying a real-world reference or the degree of fidelity wanted

skill_gaps.name: no channel for non-spatial asks
skill_gaps.why: earning coins is the entire loop, but the handoff carries only image and layout streams, so the currency itself survives only as a note

skill_gaps.name: request is a system not a map
skill_gaps.why: the user asked for a motorcycle system with realistic handling and a wheelie; the skill can only answer with a place to ride, and there is no field that records that most of the request routes elsewhere

skill_gaps.name: quiz genre ambiguity
skill_gaps.why: Puzzle offers a Word / Quiz preset and simultaneously tells you to send physical-element-free quizzes to Party & Casual, so two rules point at two files for the same prompt; following the boundary note then lands on a Quiz preset whose answer-tile floor is wrong for a typed answer, which means neither route produces a clean result
